title: Essential Verb - {pouvoir} (can)
description: Express what you can do! Master abilities through active recall and composition practice!
can_do: Express ability and possibility (I can, you can, they can)
Ask for permission politely in French
Combine with vouloir to say 'I can want' or 'Can you have?'

concepts.definition: The verb for what someone can do: ability, chance and permission. It is one of the verbs French uses most.

examples.fr: Je peux avoir ça, s'il vous plaît ?
Je peux avoir ça, s'il te plaît ?

concepts.definition: The stem changes three times: once for the singular, once for we and you, and once for they.
Put a second verb straight after {pouvoir} to say what someone can do.

mistakes.feedback: Je takes '{peux}', not 'peut'. Remember: je peux, il peut
That's 'you can', not 'I can'. Focus on the pronoun!
Tu takes '{peux}', not 'peut'. Pattern: je peux, tu peux
Il takes '{peut}', not 'peux'. Remember: il peut, elle peut
Elle takes '{peut}', not 'peux'. Same as il peut

items.hint: Conjugate '{pouvoir}' in the present for '{nous}' (regular -ons ending).

mistakes.feedback: Nous takes '{pouvons}', not 'peux'. Completely different!
Nous takes '{pouvons}', not 'peut'. Regular -ons pattern!

items.hint: Conjugate '{pouvoir}' in the present for '{vous}' (regular -ez ending).

mistakes.feedback: Vous takes '{pouvez}', not 'peux'. Regular -ez pattern!
Vous takes '{pouvez}', not 'peut'. Remember: vous pouvez
Ils takes '{peuvent}', not 'peux'. Irregular ending!
Ils takes '{peuvent}', not 'peut'. Plural form!
Elles takes '{peuvent}', not 'peux'. Same as ils peuvent
Elles takes '{peuvent}', not 'peut'. Plural form!

items.situation: Say that you can have that
items.hint: Start with 'I can' in French, then add infinitive '{avoir}' + 'that'.

mistakes.feedback: Je takes '{peux}', not 'peut'. Remember: je peux, il peut
This needs pouvoir! Try: je peux avoir ça

items.hint: Start with 'he can' in French, then add infinitive '{avoir}' + 'a book'.

mistakes.feedback: Il takes '{peut}', not 'peux'. Remember: il peut, elle peut
This needs pouvoir! Try: il peut avoir un livre

items.hint: Start with 'we can' in French, then add infinitive '{avoir}' + 'a house'.

mistakes.feedback: Nous takes '{pouvons}', not 'peux'. Completely different!
This needs pouvoir! Try: nous pouvons avoir une maison

items.hint: Use '{pouvoir}' in the present for '{je}' + infinitive '{être}' + 'a friend'.

mistakes.feedback: This needs pouvoir! Try: je peux être un ami
When you use two verbs together, the second one stays in the infinitive. Here: je peux être un ami.

items.hint: Use '{pouvoir}' in the present for '{elle}' + infinitive '{être}' + a profession.

mistakes.feedback: The English says 'can be', so you need '{pouvoir}' + infinitive: elle peut être artiste.
In French you usually drop the article with professions, and for 'she' you’d say '{une artiste}' if you use an article at all.

items.situation: Your friend asks if a cat is allowed. Say yes, she can have one.
items.hint: Use {tu peux}, then {avoir} as it is.

mistakes.feedback: This needs {pouvoir}: {tu peux avoir un chat}.
After {pouvoir} the second verb stays as it is: {tu peux avoir un chat}.

items.situation: Say that they are allowed to have a dog.
items.hint: Use {ils peuvent}, then {avoir} as it is.

mistakes.feedback: This needs {pouvoir}: {ils peuvent avoir un chien}.
{ils} takes {peuvent}: {ils peuvent avoir un chien}.
